results.reason: The response quotes Supply Agreement §14.2, including the >50% change-of-control trigger, the prior written consent requirement and the 30-day termination right. It notes that Schedule 4.4 states 'None'. It also explains that §7.2(c) covers only consents listed on Schedule 4.4, so the schedule must be corrected for the condition to reach Vantrell.
Issue G identifies §16.1: the Supplier may assign freely while the Customer needs consent. It flags the risk of assignment to a competitor or a less reliable supplier.
Issue A computes the 120-day deadline as September 2, 2026 and notes the SPA was dated September 21, 2026. It concludes the agreement will expire and refers to the Extension Pricing in Schedule B.
Issue C quotes Side Letter §2 ('solely Sections 4.1 and 4.2') and cites §11.11 precedence. It explains that 4.3 and 4.12 become subject to the $8.45M cap and the deductible.
Issue D identifies the Side Letter's Delaware law and Chancery forum against SPA §11.8/§11.9 (New York). It explains that precedence splits indemnification disputes from other disputes.
States the cap is $8,450,000 (10% of Purchase Price).
States that §11.11 gives the Side Letter first priority over the SPA.
Formatted as a memorandum to the Partner. Each issue is a distinct item listing the documents and sections, the significance to Halvorsen and a recommended action.
Opens with 'Issues Requiring Immediate Client Call' and orders the additional issues by significance. It includes a summary table of client call items.
States the deadline has passed. It does not suggest the option remains exercisable, apart from asking to confirm whether notice was delivered earlier.
States that Capitalization and Taxes are now subject to the cap and that the Side Letter controls. It makes no contrary statement.
